recipe: Use TypeScript types (rather than just runtime values) to encode the game logic of your application, so the type system enforces invariants at compile time.
trigger_condition: When building a game or logic system in TypeScript where you want compile-time guarantees about valid states and transitions.
evidence: Your goal for this challenge is to use TypeScript types to encode the game logic of Tic Tac Toe.
source_name: TypeHero: Advent of TypeScript 2023, Day Twenty One

recipe: Model the game board as a 3x3 grid where each cell can hold one of two player marks, and represent the win condition as three in a row.
trigger_condition: When modeling a two-player board game with a fixed grid size and a simple win condition.
evidence: players alternate marking `❌`s and `⭕`s in a 3x3 grid, aiming to get three in a row.
source_name: TypeHero: Advent of TypeScript 2023, Day Twenty One

recipe: Constrain your type-level outcome so that every possible terminal state is either a win for one player or a draw, eliminating any other possibility.
trigger_condition: When designing a type system for a finite game where all terminal outcomes are known and exhaustive.
evidence: Eventually, every game will end with one of the players winning or a draw.
source_name: TypeHero: Advent of TypeScript 2023, Day Twenty One
